[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/stockx-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/stockx-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product listing data from StockX.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape StockX e-commerce Data with Python](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-stockx)
- **Code:** [`stockx.py`](stockx.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Product pages](results/product.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- StockX product data
- StockX product search

## Functions

- `scrape_product(url)` → `Dict`: scrape a single stockx product page for product data
- `scrape_search(url, max_pages=25)` → `List[Dict]`: Scrape StockX search

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import stockx


async def main():
    product = await stockx.scrape_product("https://stockx.com/nike-x-stussy-bucket-hat-black")
    search = await stockx.scrape_search("https://stockx.com/search?s=nike", max_pages=2)


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/product.json`](results/product.json): `sizeDescriptor`, `urlKey`, `id`, `productCategory`, `primaryCategory`, `primaryTitle`, `secondaryTitle`, `brand`, `title`, `model`, `description`, `contentGroup`, `listingType`, `deleted`, `gender`, `browseVerticals`, `categories`, `conditions`, `condition`, `styleId`, `editionType`, `sizeAllDescriptor`, `availableSizeConversions`, `defaultSizeConversion`, `media`, `hazardousMaterial`, `tags`, `traits`, `merchandising`, `variants`, `breadcrumbs`, `brands`, `seo`, `pricing`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `__typename`, `id`, `title`, `name`, `urlKey`, `brand`, `gender`, `description`, `model`, `condition`, `productCategory`, `browseVerticals`, `listingType`, `primaryCategory`, `uuid`, `conditions`, `categories`, `favorite`, `variants`, `media`, `traits`, `market`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`stockx.py`](stockx.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `auto_scroll` = `True`: scroll the page to load lazy content
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/stockx-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
